requirements.summary: A read gives the bit-wise majority of the three copies, their OR, whether they disagree, and the lock.
A write programs the three copies, reads them back and locks the word only when the majority is the value; a locked word refuses every further write, and bits that are set cannot be cleared.

One faulty cell in a bit position, stuck at 0 or at 1, in the data or in the lock row, is outvoted and the data copies report it; two in the same position are beyond the guarantee and the write is refused by the read-back.
A loss of power stops a pulse at once and programs nothing of it; a word cut short stays unlocked, and the same write later completes it.

After every reset the lifecycle is loaded from words 0, 1 and 2 before the register block leaves reset; a stage counts when any copy is set, a gap gives the most restrictive state, and only TEST allows writing the keys.
